analysis_scope.sampling_notes: The working copy was supplied as a shallow clone with depth 50, so historical conclusions are bounded to recent history even though Git reports this one-commit checkout as non-shallow. stated_purpose: The README describes this as a throwaway repository for safely practicing the firstmate workflow by making small changes to a deliberately minimal calculator module.

observed_capabilities.statement: The repository provides Python functions that add and subtract two supplied operands.
The minimal module can serve as a target for small practice changes such as adding a function, fixing a bug, or introducing a test.

architecture.statement: The entire implementation is a single dependency-free Python source file containing two standalone functions; there is no application entry point, package structure, persistence layer, service boundary, or external integration.

accomplishments.statement: The initial commit established an explicit disposable-practice purpose and a small, readable calculator implementation suitable for controlled workflow exercises.

gaps.statement: No automated tests verify the addition or subtraction behavior.
There is no dependency manifest, packaging metadata, setup procedure, CI workflow, or executable entry point.
The repository contains no implementation or configuration of the firstmate workflow itself; it is only a practice target for that external workflow.

risks.statement: Practice edits can silently regress the arithmetic functions because no automated verification or CI safeguard exists.
The deliberately disposable framing and absence of maintenance artifacts make this repository unsuitable as a dependable calculator library or operational project.

suggested_next_actions.statement: If the sandbox will be reused, add a minimal test file and a documented test command so workflow exercises have an objective success check.
If the firstmate exercise is complete, have the owner confirm archival rather than adding production-oriented structure to a repository explicitly designated as throwaway.

questions: Has the intended firstmate practice exercise been completed?
Should the sandbox remain available for repeated workflow drills or be archived?
If it remains available, should a small automated test suite define the baseline behavior participants must preserve?
